---
title: "arrange() with a column name as text sorts nothing"
ref: TDY-06
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "the students sorted by grade"
versions: "All versions of {dplyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

grades <- data.frame(student = c("Hugo", "Nina", "Paul"), grade = c(12, 8, 15))
sort_col <- "grade"
arrange(grades, sort_col)
arrange(grades, "grade")
```
:::

## Why

`arrange()` sorts by the value of the expressions it is given. `sort_col` is not a column: it is a variable holding the string `"grade"`, the same for every row. Sorting by a constant changes nothing, and no error flags it.

The typical case is Shiny: `arrange(data, input$column)` receives the name picked by the user as text, and the displayed table is never sorted.

## The fix

Turn the text into a column with `.data[[ ]]`.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

arrange(grades, .data[[sort_col]])
arrange(grades, desc(.data[[sort_col]]))
```
:::
